X.note: The terrain relief is attractive. The 'To foreign owners / our read' label is a faded, low-contrast ghost box, and the arrow lines run through it. The 'our read' caption is tiny and unreadable on a phone. The stray fan of lines going into open sea doesn't show where the ships go or who the owners are. The map is cropped to a coastline with no country context, and 'South Korea' is placed inland, away from the point being made. The white border glow is odd. The subtitle and source line are legible.

Y.note: The globe render is strong, with good lighting and relief. Texas is highlighted in orange, so the place is obvious right away. The callout is high-contrast with a clear accent bar and dot. The date badge, subtitle and source line are all legible. The callout text is somewhat small for a phone and the callout box covers part of the central US. The subtitle says 'cities' while the callout is about Texas, a mild mismatch, and the source line is small.

why: Y shows one highlighted place with one crisp, readable callout, while X's key label is faded and illegible and its route lines don't communicate anything.
top_fix_for_weaker: Make the 'To foreign owners' label fully opaque with a high-contrast dark background, bigger text and no lines crossing it. Drop the vague 'our read' sub-label. Redraw the route as a few clear arrows ending at labelled destination countries, and zoom out so Korea and those destinations are visible together.
